mainTopic: How a handle (יד) and a protective covering (שומר) count for טומאה, starting from the hide of a נבלה, and the sources for each rule.
overview: This amud is about how parts attached to food or to a נבלה count for טומאה. It opens by finishing a ברייתא about the hide of a נבלה. רבא explains that the hide does not join with the meat to make a כזית, but when a full כזית of meat is on it, the hide acts as a handle (יד), so touching it makes a person טמא. The גמרא then quotes a משנה with three levels. A יד passes on טומאה but does not count toward the measure. A שומר (protective covering) passes on טומאה and also counts toward the measure. Something that is neither has no part in טומאה. The word ״לכם״ in the פסוקים teaches that handles count, and a קל וחומר teaches that a שומר does too, which leaves the שומר פסוק free to teach joining. Through a long back-and-forth about which handle פסוק is extra, including the rule of דיו, the גמרא settles on three sources. A יד brings טומאה in, a יד carries טומאה out, and a שומר joins with the food.

steps.title: The ending of the ברייתא: touching the hide behind the meat makes you impure
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that someone who touches the outside of the hide, right behind the meat, might stay טהור. It then uses the word ״יטמא״ to teach that he becomes טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that someone who touches the back of the hide, opposite the meat, is not impure. So the פסוק says: "shall be impure."
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last line of a ברייתא about the hide of a נבלה. It says that touching the outside of the hide, right behind the meat, makes a person טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not touch the meat itself. He only touched the hide from the outside, at the spot facing the meat. The ברייתא learns from the word ״יטמא״ that he is still טמא. This seems to clash with the beginning of the ברייתא, which used ״בנבלתה״ to leave out the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have thought..." It introduces an idea that the ברייתא is about to reject.
On the outside of the hide, at the spot directly behind the meat
"The פסוק teaches us." It brings the word in the פסוק that settles the question.
"Shall be impure" (ויקרא 11:39)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the ברייתא. The beginning, which uses ״בנבלתה״ to exclude the hide, came just before this section. That is why the next step asks how the two halves fit together.

phrases.english: One might think: one who touches opposite the meat, from its back side
phrases.notes: He touches the outer side of the hide, right where the meat is attached on the inside.

phrases.english: would not be impure?
The verse teaches: "shall be impure."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל הַנּוֹגֵעַ כְּנֶגֶד בָּשָׂר מֵאֲחוֹרָיו לֹא יְהֵא טָמֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Touching the outside of a נבלה's hide, opposite the meat, makes a person טמא, learned from ״יטמא״.

steps.title: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא really means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא is saying. Its first half excludes the hide, but its ending includes the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the ברייתא means, because its two halves seem to contradict each other. This question sets up the next step, where רבא explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בנבלתה״ seemed to say that the hide does not pass on טומאת נבלה. ״יטמא״ seems to say that it does. The question is how the same ברייתא can say both things.

keyTerms.meaning: "What is it saying?" Used when a text seems unclear or self-contradicting.

phrases.english: What is it saying?
phrases.notes: He means: the start of the ברייתא leaves out the hide, and the end includes it. How do they fit?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions how the ending in step 1 fits with the beginning of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the ברייתא both exclude the hide (״בנבלתה״) and include it (״יטמא״)?
steps.kashyaTarget: The internal consistency of the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first half says the hide is not like the meat, and the second half says touching it makes you טמא.

steps.title: Words are missing: the hide does not join with the meat to make a כזית
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or an unnamed teacher) says the ברייתא has words missing. Its first rule is that ״בנבלתה״ leaves out a hide without a כזית of meat on it, even if the hide would bring the meat up to a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say it without naming anyone: Words are missing, and this is what it teaches. "Its carcass," but not a hide that does not have an olive's worth of meat on it, even if the hide would complete it to an olive's worth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to answer the question. He says the ברייתא is missing words, and he rewrites its first half correctly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ״בנבלתה״ does not mean the hide never matters. It means the hide cannot be added to the meat to reach the minimum size of a כזית. So a little meat plus hide that together come to a כזית is not enough to make someone טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is missing words." The text needs words filled in to be understood correctly.
"And this is what it teaches." It introduces the corrected wording.
The size of an olive, the minimum amount of נבלה that passes on טומאה
Completes it, making up the missing amount
The hide (skin) of the animal

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it unattributed:
It is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
"Its carcass" — but not a hide
that does not have an olive's worth of meat on it,
and the hide completes it to an olive's worth.
phrases.notes: Even with the hide counted in, the total does not count as a כזית.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַסּוֹרֵי מִיחַסְּרָא וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 by filling in missing words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ״בנבלתה״ seemed to exclude the hide from טומאה completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: ״בנבלתה″ only teaches that the hide does not join with the meat to make up a כזית.

steps.title: With a full כזית of meat, the hide works as a handle
steps.stepSummary: The corrected ברייתא continues. If there is a full כזית of meat on the hide, touching the outside of the hide makes you טמא, because the hide counts as a handle (יד) for the meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think that I also leave out a hide that has an olive's worth of meat on it. Then someone who touches the back of the hide, opposite the meat, would not be impure, and the hide would not even act as a handle. So the פסוק says: "shall be impure."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes rebuilding the ברייתא. This shows that the ending (״יטמא״) is about a different case from the beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The beginning was about adding the hide to make up a כזית, and that does not work. The ending is about a hide with a full כזית of meat already on it. There, the hide counts as a handle, and touching a handle is like touching the meat itself. So there is no contradiction, because the two halves teach two different jobs of the hide.

keyTerms.meaning: Exclude, leave out of the rule
Acting as a handle. Touching it passes on the טומאה as if you touched the food itself.
Does not act as, does not count as

steps.whatToRemember: The hide of a נבלה has two separate rules. (1) It does not join with the meat to make up a כזית (״בנבלתה״). (2) When a full כזית of meat is on it, it does act as a handle, so touching it from outside makes you טמא (״יטמא״).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up "joining to make a size" with "acting as a handle." The hide fails at the first and succeeds at the second. That is how both halves of the ברייתא can be true.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a pattern in the laws of טומאה. One part of a food can count for one job, like being a handle, without counting for another job, like adding to the minimum size.

phrases.english: One might think that I exclude even a hide
that has an olive's worth of meat on it,
so one who touches opposite the meat, from its back side,
one might think he would not be impure,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ מַעֲשֵׂה יָד נָמֵי לָא עָבֵיד.
phrases.english: and that it does not even act as a handle.
phrases.notes: A handle (יד) is a part you can hold the food by. Touching it counts like touching the meat.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "shall be impure."

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מוֹצִיא אַף עוֹר שֶׁיֵּשׁ עָלָיו כְּזַיִת בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the rebuilt ברייתא started in step 3 and explains the ending from step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (different amount of meat, different job of the hide)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the hide does not join to make a כזית, one might think it does not even count as a handle.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a full כזית of meat on it, the hide is a handle, so touching it from outside makes a person טמא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The hide does not join to make up a כזית, but it does act as a handle for a full כזית of meat.

steps.title: A handle that does not protect: it passes on טומאה but does not count toward the measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה elsewhere. Anything that is only a handle (יד) and not a protective covering (שומר) becomes טמא and makes other things טמא, but it does not join the food to make up the needed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: anything that is a handle but not a protective covering becomes טמא and makes things טמא, but it does not join with the food to make up the measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings a general rule about handles from another משנה. It connects to the last step, which called the hide a יד for the meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handle is a part you hold the food by, like a stem. If the handle touches something טמא, the food becomes טמא. If someone touches the handle of טמא food, he becomes טמא. But the handle does not count as part of the food's size.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle: a part you hold the food by, like a stem
A protective covering, like a shell or peel, that guards the food
Becomes טמא itself and makes other things טמא
Joins together with the food to reach the needed measure

steps.confusionAlert: Passing on טומאה and counting toward the measure are two separate things. A יד does the first but not the second.

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: "There" means in a different מסכת. This משנה is the first one in מסכת עוקצין.

phrases.english: Anything that is a handle but not a protective covering –
becomes טמא and makes other things טמא,
but it does not join together with the food.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 4 called the hide a יד for the meat. This step brings the general משנה about how a יד works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A יד that is not a שומר becomes טמא and passes on טומאה, but does not count toward the measure.

steps.title: A protective covering counts toward the measure; something that is neither has no part in טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues. A שומר, even if it is not a handle, becomes טמא, passes on טומאה, and does join with the food toward the measure. Something that is neither a handle nor a covering does not become טמא and does not pass on טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A protective covering, even if it is not a handle, becomes טמא, makes things טמא, and joins with the food. Something that is not a handle and not a covering does not become טמא and does not make things טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list with two more types: the protective covering, and something that is neither a handle nor a covering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שומר is treated more strongly than a יד. Like a יד, it passes on טומאה, but it also counts as part of the food's size. A part that neither holds nor protects the food is treated like it is not connected to the food at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though it is not a handle
Neither a handle nor a protective covering
Does not become טמא and does not make other things טמא

steps.whatToRemember: Three levels: a שומר passes on טומאה and counts toward the measure. A יד passes on טומאה but does not count. Something that is neither has no part in טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: שׁוֹמֵר, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָד –
phrases.english: A protective covering, even though it is not a handle –
becomes טמא, makes things טמא, and joins together;
not a handle and not a protective covering –
does not become טמא and does not make things טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוֹמֵר, וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה that step 5 began by adding the שומר and the 'neither' cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר becomes טמא, passes on טומאה, and counts toward the measure. Something that is neither a יד nor a שומר has no part in טומאה.

steps.title: Where does the תורה teach that handles count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק teaches the rule that ידות become טמא and pass on טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where is the rule about handles written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה for the handle rule. This sets up the next two steps, which bring פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated the rule about ידות without giving a source. The גמרא now wants the source in the Torah for treating a handle like part of the food for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Handles (the plural of יד)
Where are they written? A request for the source in the Torah

phrases.english: Handles, where are they written?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָדוֹת הֵיכָא כְּתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the יד rule stated in step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that ידות become טמא and pass on טומאה.

steps.title: First source: ״לָכֶם״ in the פסוק about food becoming טמא
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a נבלה falling on wet seeds says ״טמא הוא לכם״. The word ״לכם״, meaning 'for you', includes everything you need when using the food, so handles are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'If water is put on seed, and any of their carcass falls on it, it is טמא for you.' 'For you' means everything you need, which includes the handles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first Torah source for handles. It reads the word ״לכם״ as including the parts you need to use the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is about food receiving טומאה. ״לכם״ teaches that whatever you need to handle the food, like a stem you hold it by, is treated as part of the food. So if the handle touches the נבלה, the food becomes טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Seed, here standing for food
The carcass of an animal that died without proper שחיטה, which is a source of טומאה
To everything that you need
To include: an extra word teaches that something more is covered

phrases.english: As it is written: 'But if water is put on seed,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:38

phrases.english: and any of their carcass falls on it,
it is טמא for you.'
'For you' means for everything that you need,
to include the handles.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב ״וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 7's question with a first פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לכם״ in the פסוק about food receiving טומאה includes the parts you need to use the food, which are the ידות.

steps.title: Second source: ״לָכֶם״ about the נבלה, so a handle works both ways
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק, about an animal that dies, also says ״לכם״, again including handles. Together the two פסוקים teach that a handle brings טומאה in and also passes it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'If any animal which is for you dies.' 'For you' means everything you need, which includes the handles. So a handle works to bring טומאה in and to bring it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק with the same word ״לכם״ and then sums up what the two פסוקים teach together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק was about food receiving טומאה through its handle (bringing in). This פסוק is about a נבלה giving טומאה out, so touching the handle of something טמא makes you טמא (bringing out). That is why the hide, as a יד for the meat, makes the person who touches it טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal
To bring in: the handle lets טומאה come into the food
To bring out: the handle lets טומאה go out from the food to others

steps.whatToRemember: A יד works both ways, a rule learned from two separate ״לכם״ פסוקים. It brings טומאה into the food, and it passes טומאה from the food to whoever touches it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains step 4: the hide is a יד for the meat, so touching the hide passes the meat's טומאה to the person.

phrases.english: And it is written: 'And if any animal dies'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:39

phrases.english: which is for you,'
'For you' means for everything that you need,
to include the handles,
a handle to bring in and to bring out.
phrases.notes: One פסוק teaches that טומאה comes in through the handle, and the other teaches that it goes out through the handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״וְכִי יָמוּת מִן הַבְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר הִיא לָכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to the one in step 8 and draws the shared conclusion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״לכם״ in the נבלה פסוק also includes ידות. Together with the first פסוק, this shows a יד both brings טומאה in and brings it out.

steps.title: A covering's טומאה comes from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says no פסוק is needed to teach that a שומר brings in and passes out טומאה, since a קל וחומר from a יד proves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A covering does not need a verse to teach that it brings טומאה in and passes it out. We learn it from a handle: if a handle, which does not even protect the food, brings in and passes out טומאה, then a covering, which does protect it, surely does too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds on what it just learned about handles. It says the same rule for a שומר can be worked out by logic alone, without a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A handle is the weaker connection to the food, because it does not protect it. A covering is the stronger connection, because it guards the food. If the weaker one already brings טומאה in and passes it out, the stronger one surely does too. This sets up the next question: why did the Torah write a פסוק about שומר at all?

keyTerms.meaning: A protective covering of a food, like a shell or peel
To bring טומאה in: if the attachment touches טומאה, the food becomes טמא
To pass טומאה out: if the food is טמא, touching the attachment makes other things טמא
Logic from weaker to stronger: if a weaker thing has a rule, a stronger thing surely has it
Protects or shields

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. 'Bringing in' means טומאה from outside reaches the food through the attachment. 'Passing out' means טומאה from the food reaches other things through the attachment.

phrases.english: A covering, to bring in and to pass out [טומאה] —
does not need a verse;
it comes through a קל וחומר from a handle:
If a handle, which does not protect [the food] —
brings in and passes out [טומאה],
phrases.notes: We know this from steps 8 and 9, the two פסוקים that say ״לכם״.

phrases.english: then a covering, not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר מִיָּד אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the rule just derived for יד as the base for a קל וחומר to שומר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שומר brings in and passes out טומאה through a קל וחומר from יד, with no פסוק needed.

steps.title: Why did the תורה write about the covering?
steps.stepSummary: If logic already teaches the covering's טומאה, the גמרא asks what the פסוק about שומר is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: The covering that the תורה wrote about, why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the Torah needed a פסוק about שומר if the קל וחומר already teaches it. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a basic rule that the Torah does not write a פסוק for nothing. Since the קל וחומר covers bringing in and passing out, the פסוק about שומר must be teaching something extra.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the Torah
'Why do I need it?' Used when a source seems unnecessary

phrases.english: The covering that the Torah wrote about,
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק about seeds that are sown (ויקרא 11:37), which teaches that a covering counts with the food.

phrases.english: why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 10: if logic already teaches it, the פסוק seems extra.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new rule the פסוק about שומר teaches beyond the קל וחומר.

steps.title: The פסוק teaches that a covering joins the food
steps.stepSummary: The extra פסוק teaches that a שומר joins with the food to make up the needed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from it that a covering joins together with the food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The פסוק about שומר is there to teach the one rule a handle does not have: joining.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains the difference in the משנה from step 6. A handle brings in and passes out טומאה but does not join the food toward the needed amount. A covering does all three. The extra joining rule comes from the extra פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from it'. Draws a conclusion
To join: the covering counts together with the food to reach the needed amount for טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: יד brings in and passes out טומאה (from ״לכם״). שומר does the same by קל וחומר. The פסוק about שומר adds that it also joins the food toward the measure.

phrases.english: Learn from it that it joins together [with the food toward the measure].

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ לְצָרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק about שומר teaches that a שומר joins the food toward the required amount.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוקים should be split differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another reading: a handle only brings in, a covering brings in and passes out, and nobody joins.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: a handle brings טומאה in but does not pass it out, and a covering brings it in and passes it out. But a handle passing out, and a covering joining, we would not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reading it just gave. Maybe the two sources should be split up so that neither 'a handle passes out' nor 'a covering joins' is learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the ״לכם״ פסוקים give a handle only bringing in. The פסוק about שומר is then used up teaching that a covering brings in and passes out. That would leave nothing to teach joining, so the conclusion of step 12 would fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But say'. Offers a different possible reading as a challenge
But

phrases.english: But say [instead]:
a handle brings in but does not pass out,
a covering brings in and passes out,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל יָד לְהוֹצִיא וְשׁוֹמֵר לְצָרֵף – לָא.
phrases.english: but a handle to pass out, and a covering to join, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading that produced step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the פסוק about שומר teaches joining (לצרף).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a handle only brings in, the קל וחומר gives a covering only bringing in. Then the פסוק about שומר is needed for passing out, and nothing is left to teach joining.

steps.title: A handle that brings in surely passes out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that a handle only brings in, because bringing in is the bigger thing, so passing out surely follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say a handle brings in but does not pass out. Now, if it even brings טומאה in, does it need to be said that it passes it out?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Once a handle brings טומאה into the food, it obviously also passes טומאה out of the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making clean food become טמא through a handle is the bigger thing. Letting food that is already טמא spread its טומאה through the handle is smaller. So a handle does both, the קל וחומר gives a covering both, and the פסוק about שומר stays free to teach joining.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You cannot say'. Rejects a suggested reading
'Now', meaning 'if even this is so'. Opens a 'surely then' argument
'Is it needed?' Means it is obvious

steps.whatToRemember: Since a handle surely passes out טומאה if it brings it in, the קל וחומר to שומר holds. The extra פסוק therefore teaches that a שומר joins the food toward the measure.

phrases.english: A handle brings in but does not pass out:
you cannot say that,
now that it brings [טומאה] in,
is passing it out even a question?!
phrases.notes: If the handle can make clean food טמא, it can surely carry the food's own טומאה out to other things.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 and restores step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical rejection of the suggested split, using a 'surely then' argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A handle might only bring טומאה in, which would use up the פסוק about שומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Bringing in is the bigger thing, so a handle also passes out. The קל וחומר covers שומר for both, and the פסוק about שומר teaches joining.

steps.title: Maybe a handle only passes out, and a covering never joins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the earlier suggestion. Maybe a יד only passes out טומאה, a שומר passes out and brings in, and a שומר does not join with the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: a handle passes out טומאה but does not bring it in. A covering passes out and brings in. But a handle bringing in, or a covering joining with the food, we do not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: Step 14 rejected the idea that a handle only brings in. Now the גמרא tries the opposite: maybe a handle only passes out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the weaker job, passing out, is given to the handle, so the logic from step 14 does not knock it down. Then the extra שומר verse would be used to make a covering stronger than a handle, giving it both directions. Nothing would be left to teach that a covering joins.

keyTerms.meaning: A handle, like a stem attached to a fruit
A protective covering, like a shell or peel
To pass out: if the food becomes טמא, the טומאה goes out through the handle to whoever touches it
To bring in: if the handle touches טומאה, the טומאה goes into the food
To join: the covering counts toward the minimum amount of food needed

steps.confusionAlert: This is the reverse of step 13. There a handle only brought in. Here a handle only passes out. Keep track of which direction is given to the handle.

phrases.english: But say instead:
a handle passes out but does not bring in,
a covering passes out and brings in,
but a handle bringing in
and a covering joining: no.
phrases.notes: He means we would not learn either of these two things at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 knocked out the version where a handle only brings in, this offers the reverse version, which step 14's logic does not refute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 12 that the extra שומר verse teaches joining.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a handle has only one source, it may do only the weaker job, passing out. The שומר verse would then be needed to make a covering do both jobs, and joining would have no source.

steps.title: An extra verse about handles comes from vessels
steps.stepSummary: There is another פסוק that teaches about handles: the verse about an oven and range. Its word לכם includes everything you need for using the vessel, which means handles.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is an extra verse written about a handle: "An oven and a range shall be broken..." The word "for you" means everything that you need, which includes the handles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a handle has a second source, from the verse about vessels. So a handle gets both jobs, passing out and bringing in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two sources, one teaches that a handle passes out and the other that it brings in. Then a קל וחומר gives a covering both jobs too. That frees the extra שומר verse to teach that a covering joins with the food, as step 12 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Extra, an additional source
An oven and a cooking range, from the verse about vessels becoming טמא
Everything you need for using it
To include something more in the law

steps.whyThisMatters: This restores the conclusion of step 12: a handle brings in and passes out, a covering does both, and a covering also joins with the food.

phrases.english: an extra verse is written about a handle,
"an oven and a range shall be broken, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 11:35. The verse ends with "they shall be טמא for you," which is where the next word comes from.

phrases.english: "for you":
for everything that you need,
to include the handles.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָד יַתִּירָא כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15 by showing that handles have a second source.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings an additional פסוק so the handle has two sources and covers both jobs.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A handle has only one source, so it might only pass out, and the שומר verse would be used up.
steps.terutzMaskana: A handle has an extra source, so it passes out and brings in. A covering learns both by קל וחומר, and its own verse teaches joining.

steps.title: Which handle verse is really extra?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the answer: of the verses that teach about handles, which one is truly extra? Each may be needed for its own area.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which of them is extra?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 16's claim of an extra verse. This short question sets up the next move: steps 18 to 20 sharpen it, and step 21 answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The handle verses come from different areas, such as food and vessels. Each one may be needed to teach that handles pass out טומאה in its own area. If so, none is free to teach bringing in, and step 16's answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one of them
Is extra, not needed for its own teaching

phrases.english: Which of them is extra?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the different verses that teach about handles, including the oven verse just quoted.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי מִינַּיְיהוּ מְיַיתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 16's claim that one of the handle verses is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 16's claim that the oven verse gives handles an extra source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each handle verse may be needed for its own area of טומאה, so none is left over to teach that a handle brings in.

steps.title: Trying to learn everything from the seeds verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests writing the handle rule only for זרעים (food) and learning the rest from it, then rejects this because food has a stronger kind of טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write the rule only about seeds (food), and learn the others from it. No: seeds are special, because their טומאה is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins showing why no single פסוק seems extra. It tests the seeds פסוק first and knocks it down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the food פסוק alone could teach vessels and carcasses, the other two פסוקים would be extra. But food takes on טומאה more easily than the others, so a rule said about food might not carry over to weaker areas. That makes the food פסוק unable to teach the rest.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Torah (the Merciful One) write it here
Seeds; here it stands for food and its טומאה
What about...? The opening of a rejection that points out what makes one case special
Their טומאה is greater: they become טמא more easily

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking whether handles pass on טומאה. That is already settled. It is only asking which of the three פסוקים is not needed for its own area.

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write it regarding seeds
phrases.notes: Meaning: let the Torah teach the handle rule only in the פסוק about food.

phrases.english: and let those others be learned from them
phrases.notes: "Those others" are vessels and carcasses.

phrases.english: But what about seeds?
They are special, for their impurity is greater.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּזְרָעִים, וְלֵיתוֹ הָנָךְ מִינַּיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the question of step 17 by testing the first פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one of the handle פסוקים is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The food פסוק cannot teach the others because food has a stronger טומאה, so it is needed for itself alone

steps.title: Trying to learn everything from the oven verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the handle rule from the תנור (vessel) פסוק alone, then rejects it because a vessel makes things טמא through its airspace.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write the rule only about an oven, and learn the others from it. No: an oven is special, because it makes things טמא from its airspace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second פסוק, the oven, and shows it too cannot teach the other areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vessel like an oven can make food inside it טמא even without touching, just through the air inside it. Food and carcasses do not have this strength, so a rule from the oven might not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven; here it stands for vessels and their טומאה
Makes things טמא through its airspace, without touching

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write it regarding an oven
and let those others be learned from it
phrases.notes: Here "those others" are food and carcasses.

phrases.english: But what about an oven?
It is special, for it makes things impure from its airspace.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּתַנּוּר, וְלֵיתֵי הָנָךְ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same test as step 18, now on the oven פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one of the handle פסוקים is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The oven פסוק cannot teach the others because vessels pass on טומאה through their airspace, a strength the others lack

steps.title: Trying to learn everything from the carcass verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning the handle rule from the נבלה פסוק alone, then rejects it because a carcass has three special strengths.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the Torah write the rule only about a carcass, and learn the others from it. No: a carcass is special, because it makes a person טמא, it makes טמא by carrying, and its טומאה comes from its own body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the third פסוק, the carcass, and rejects it as well. Now all three seem needed, which makes the question of step 17 strong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נבלה is stronger in three ways: it can make a person טמא, it can make someone טמא just by carrying it, and its טומאה starts from itself, not from something else. Food and vessels lack these, so the carcass cannot teach them.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה; a carcass
Makes someone טמא by carrying it, even without touching
Its טומאה comes from its own body, not from an outside source

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One write it regarding a carcass
and let those others be learned from it
phrases.notes: Now "those others" are food and vessels.

phrases.english: But what about a carcass?
It is special, for it makes a person impure,
and it makes impure through carrying,
and its impurity comes out from its own body.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּנְבֵלָה, וְלֵיתֵי הָנָךְ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the test of all three פסוקים begun in step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one of the handle פסוקים is extra
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The carcass פסוק cannot teach the others because a carcass has three stringencies the others lack, so every פסוק appears needed

steps.title: One cannot come from one, but one can come from two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that although no single area can teach another, any two together can teach the third, so one פסוק is still extra.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cannot be learned from one, but let one be learned from two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of steps 17 to 20. It agrees no single פסוק can teach another, but says two together can teach the third.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each area alone has a special strength that blocks learning from it. But when two areas both have the handle rule, the special strength of one is missing in the other, so the rule cannot depend on those strengths, and it carries over to the third area. That makes the third פסוק extra, free to teach something else.

keyTerms.meaning: One cannot be learned from one
Let one be learned from two together

steps.whatToRemember: Each kind of טומאה (food, vessels, carcass) has its own stringency, so none can teach another alone. But any two together can teach the third, so one of the three handle פסוקים is extra.
steps.whyThisMatters: This saves the earlier answer (step 16): there really is an extra פסוק about handles, so it can be used to teach something new.

phrases.english: One cannot be learned from one;
let one be learned from two.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question built up in steps 17 to 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Learning from two sources together instead of one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since each area has its own stringency, every פסוק is needed and none is extra
steps.terutzMaskana: Two areas together can teach the third, so one פסוק is extra

steps.title: Which one can be learned from the other two? Trying food first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which area can be learned from the other two, and suggests that the תורה did not need to write the handle rule for זרעים, since it could be learned from vessels and נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one can be derived? Let the תורה not write the handle rule for זרעים (food), and we will learn it from those other two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts testing step 21's claim. It suggests that the food פסוק is the extra one, because food could be learned from vessels and נבלה together. The next step will check whether this works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 said any two can teach the third. Now the גמרא must show which specific פסוק that leaves extra. It starts with food: if vessels and נבלה both have the handle rule, maybe food follows from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Which one can be derived? (Which area can we learn from the others?)
Let the תורה not write it, since it could be learned another way
Seeds; here standing for food in the laws of טומאה

phrases.english: Which can be derived?
Let the Merciful One not write it regarding seeds,
and let it be derived from those!
phrases.notes: "Those" are the other two areas: vessels (the oven) and the carcass (נבלה).

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי תֵּיתֵי? לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּזְרָעִים, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts step 21's claim to the test by proposing that the food פסוק is the extra one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the three handle פסוקים can be learned from the other two and is therefore extra?

steps.title: Rejected: food needs הכשר before it can become טמא
steps.stepSummary: Vessels and נבלה can become טמא without הכשר, but food can become טמא only after הכשר, so food cannot be learned from them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about those two? They become טמא without הכשר. Can you say the same about food, which becomes טמא only after הכשר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning food from the other two. Vessels and נבלה are stricter, because they don't need הכשר, so their rule may not carry over to food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To learn from two cases, the new case must not be weaker in a way both of them lack. Food is weaker here: it can become טמא only after liquid has made it ready (הכשר). Vessels and נבלה don't need that step.

keyTerms.meaning: What about those? The opening words for showing that the source cases are special
Making food ready to become טמא, by its contact with liquid
Can you say? Questioning whether the rule carries over to the new case

phrases.english: What about those?
For they become impure without being made susceptible.
Shall you say the same regarding seeds,
which become impure only after being made susceptible!
phrases.notes: Food can become טמא only after it has first gotten wet with one of the liquids that make it ready.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ – שֶׁכֵּן מִטַּמְּאִין שֶׁלֹּא בְּהֶכְשֵׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of step 22.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The derivation of food's handle rule from vessels and נבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both source cases become טמא without הכשר, a strictness that food lacks.

steps.title: רב הונא: unready produce is like an unfinished oven
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע says the הכשר point doesn't separate food from vessels: food that hasn't had הכשר is like an oven that isn't finished, which also can't become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע said: Produce that has not had הכשר is like an oven whose building is not finished.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא pushes back against the rejection in step 23. He shows that vessels also have a stage before they can become טמא, so the הכשר difference is not real.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven can become טמא only once it is finished. That is like food needing הכשר first. So vessels and food are alike on this point, and the step 23 rejection falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce that has not been made ready to become טמא
Its making is finished; a vessel becomes able to be טמא only once it is complete
Is like, is the same as

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
Produce that has not been made susceptible
is like an oven whose making is not finished.
phrases.notes: An unfinished oven can't become טמא yet, just like food before it gets wet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: פֵּירוֹת שֶׁלֹּא הוּכְשְׁרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels the rejection of step 23 by showing vessels have a matching limitation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The הכשר distinction offered in step 23.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Vessels also have a stage before they can become טמא (an unfinished oven), so food is not uniquely weaker.

steps.title: A better rejection: food becomes טמא only by touching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects learning food from the other two in a new way: vessels and נבלה can become טמא without touching, but food becomes טמא only through touching.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, refute it like this: What about those two? They become טמא even without touching. Can you say the same about food, which becomes טמא only through touching?
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב הונא knocked down the first rejection, the גמרא finds a different reason why food can't be learned from vessels and נבלה. So the food פסוק is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven becomes טמא when a שרץ is inside its airspace, with no touching. A נבלה is טמא from its own body. Food becomes טמא only by touching something טמא, so it is weaker, and the derivation fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, refute it this way. The גמרא swaps in a better rejection
Touching; direct contact with something טמא

steps.whyThisMatters: The food פסוק cannot be the extra one, so the גמרא must now check the other two areas.

phrases.english: Rather, refute it like this:
What about those?
For they become impure without contact.
phrases.notes: An oven through its airspace; a נבלה is טמא from its own body.

phrases.english: Shall you say the same regarding seeds,
which become impure only through contact!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פָּרֵיךְ הָכִי: מָה לְהָנָךְ, שֶׁכֵּן מִטַּמְּאִין שֶׁלֹּא בִּנְגִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejection that רב הונא knocked down in step 24 with a stronger one.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The derivation of food's handle rule from vessels and נבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Vessels and נבלה become טמא without touching, while food becomes טמא only through touching.

steps.title: Trying the oven: learn vessels from food and נבלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now suggests that the תורה did not need to write the handle rule for the תנור, since it could be learned from food and נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה not write the handle rule for the oven, and we will learn it from those two cases.
steps.whatsHappening: Since food could not be learned, the גמרא tries the next area: maybe the vessel (oven) פסוק is extra. The next step will test this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the source cases are food and נבלה, and the case being learned is vessels. If it works, the oven פסוק would be the extra one.

keyTerms.meaning: Oven; here standing for vessels in the laws of טומאה

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write it regarding an oven,
and let it be derived from those.
phrases.notes: This time "those" are food and the carcass (נבלה).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּתַנּוּר, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After food failed in step 25, the גמרא tries the vessel area instead.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can the oven's handle rule be learned from food and נבלה, so that the oven פסוק is extra?

steps.title: Rejected: food and נבלה are both edible
steps.stepSummary: Food and נבלה are both things that are eaten, so their rule may not carry over to an oven, which is not food.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about those two? They are food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects learning the oven from food and נבלה. Both of them are food, and an oven is not, so the oven פסוק is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both source cases share one feature, being food, and the oven lacks it. That shared feature might be why they have the handle rule, so the oven can't be learned from them.

keyTerms.meaning: Food; something that is eaten

phrases.english: What about those? For they are food.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן אוֹכֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposal of step 26.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The derivation of the oven's handle rule from food and נבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Both source cases are food, a feature that the oven lacks.

steps.title: Maybe the handle rule for נבלה is not needed either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תורה did not need to write the handle rule for נבלה, since it could be learned from food and vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let the תורה not write the handle rule for נבלה, and let us learn it from those other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks the same kind of question it asked about the oven, but this time about נבלה. Why write a handle rule for נבלה, if we could learn it from food and vessels?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 26 the גמרא tried to learn the oven from food and נבלה, and that failed in step 27. Now it tries the other combination: learn נבלה from food and vessels (the oven). If this works, the handle פסוק written about נבלה becomes 'extra'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳ who wrote it
An animal that died without proper שחיטה; it is a source of טומאה
A handle; something attached to food or an item that is treated as part of it for טומאה

phrases.english: Let the Merciful One not write [the handle rule] for a נבלה,
and let it be learned from those [cases]?
phrases.notes: 'Those' means food and vessels, the two cases the גמרא has been comparing.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא לִכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בִּנְבֵלָה, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After failing to learn the oven from the other two, the גמרא tries learning נבלה from the other two.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the handle פסוק for נבלה extra, since it could be learned from food and vessels?

steps.title: Yes, so the נבלה handle verse teaches about handles in general
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the נבלה handle rule could be learned, so the extra פסוק is moved to teach about handles in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, that is right. Then why do I need the handle rule for נבלה? If it is not needed for the handle of נבלה, use it for handles in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the suggestion. Since the פסוק about the handle of נבלה is not needed for נבלה itself, it applies that פסוק to handles in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses a well-known method: when a פסוק is not needed for its own topic, we apply it to a different topic. Here the 'free' פסוק is used to teach a new rule about handles of food, that a handle can bring טומאה in.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Yes, it is indeed so', the גמרא accepts the point
'If it is not needed for this matter, apply it to another matter', a method for using an extra פסוק
A handle in general, not just the handle of a נבלה

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so.
Rather, why do I need [the פסוק about] the handle of a נבלה?
If it is not needed for the matter of the handle of a נבלה,
apply it to the matter of a handle in general.
phrases.notes: He means handles of food, so it can teach that a handle brings טומאה into the food.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין הָכִי נָמֵי. אֶלָּא יָד דִּנְבֵלָה לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the suggestion of step 28 and moves the now-extra פסוק to a new use.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, נבלה can be learned from the others, so its handle פסוק teaches about handles in general.

steps.title: Summary: what handle and protection each teach
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up: one handle source teaches bringing טומאה in, one teaches carrying it out, and the שומר source teaches joining together.
steps.simpleTranslation: A handle to bring in, a handle to carry out, and a protective covering to join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short summary of what each source now teaches, after the move in step 29.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are two handle sources: one for להכניס (if the handle touches something טמא, the food becomes טמא) and one for להוציא (a טמא food passes טומאה out through its handle). A שומר protects the food and a handle does not, so the שומר's in-and-out rules come from a קל וחומר from the handle. That leaves the שומר source free to teach לצרף, counting toward the needed size.

keyTerms.meaning: To bring טומאה in: if the handle touches something טמא, the food becomes טמא
To carry טומאה out: if the food is טמא, touching its handle makes other things טמא
A protective covering, like a peel or shell
To join together, so it counts toward the size needed for טומאה

steps.whatToRemember: Three jobs, three sources: יד brings in, יד carries out, שומר joins together.

phrases.english: A handle to bring in [טומאה], a handle to carry out [טומאה],
a protective covering to join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָד לְהַכְנִיס, יָד לְהוֹצִיא, שׁוֹמֵר לְצָרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of the derivation in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Handle brings in and carries out; protection joins together.

steps.title: The נבלה handle verse is still needed because of דיו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the handle פסוק for נבלה is needed after all, because of the rule of דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But still, the handle of נבלה is needed. If the תורה had not written it for נבלה, I would have said: it is enough for a rule that is learned to be like its source. Just as those do not make a person טמא, so too נבלה would not make a person טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 29. It says the נבלה handle פסוק is not extra at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we learned the נבלה handle from food and vessels, the rule of דיו says the learned case cannot be stronger than its source. Handles of food and vessels do not make a person טמא, so we would think the handle of a נבלה does not make a person טמא either. The פסוק is needed to teach that it does.

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough for what is learned to be like its source': a learned rule cannot be stronger than the case it came from
'I would have said', what we would have thought without the פסוק
Makes a person טמא

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether a נבלה handle passes טומאה at all. It is how strong that טומאה is: whether it reaches a person.

phrases.english: But still, [the פסוק about] the handle of a נבלה is needed,
for if the Merciful One had not written it for a נבלה,
I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן,
phrases.english: It is enough for what comes from a derivation to be like its source,
just as those do not make a person טמא,
phrases.notes: 'Those' are the handles of food and vessels, the source cases.

phrases.english: so too a נבלה [handle] would not make a person טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַכַּתִּי, יָד דִּנְבֵלָה אִצְטְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 29's claim that the נבלה handle פסוק is extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the handle פסוק for נבלה is free to teach about handles in general.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because of דיו, a learned נבלה handle could not make a person טמא, so the פסוק is needed for that stronger rule.

steps.title: It is the שומר of נבלה that is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the handle of נבלה is needed, but shows that the שומר פסוק for נבלה has no job of its own, so that is the extra one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the handle of נבלה really is needed, and it is the protective covering of נבלה that is not needed. For what law did the תורה write it? If to join together, you already said it does not join together. And to carry out, that comes from a קל וחומר from the handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by switching which פסוק is extra. It is not the handle of נבלה, but the שומר of נבלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שומר of נבלה cannot be teaching joining together, since we already know it does not join together for נבלה. It also cannot be teaching carrying out, because a שומר protects the item and a handle does not, so a קל וחומר from the handle already teaches that. So the שומר פסוק is free to be used elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning from a weaker case to a stronger case: if a handle carries טומאה out, surely a protective covering does
'For what law?', asking what a פסוק comes to teach
Joins together to make up the needed size

steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the summary of step 30 standing: there is still an extra source, it just comes from the שומר of נבלה instead of the handle of נבלה.

phrases.english: Rather, [the פסוק about] the handle of a נבלה really is needed,
and it is [the פסוק about] the protective covering of a נבלה that is not needed.
For what law did the Merciful One write it?
If to join together [to make up the size] –
you [already] said that it does not join together,
phrases.notes: This points back to step 3: the hide, which covers the meat, does not complete a כזית of נבלה.

phrases.english: and [if] to carry out [טומאה] –
that comes from a קל וחומר from a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, יָד דִּנְבֵלָה מִיצְרָךְ צְרִיךְ, וְשׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה הוּא דְּלָא צְרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 31 and finds a different extra פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The handle פסוק of נבלה was the extra one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The handle פסוק of נבלה is needed; the שומר פסוק of נבלה is the extra one, since it cannot teach joining or carrying out.

steps.title: Moving the extra verses down a chain
steps.stepSummary: The extra שומר פסוק of נבלה is given to the handle of נבלה, and then the handle פסוק of נבלה is given to handles in general.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: if the verse is not needed for the protective covering of a נבלה, use it for the handle of a נבלה. And if that is not needed for the handle of a נבלה, use it for handles in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer from step 32 by moving the extra verses, one after another, to new jobs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 showed that the שומר פסוק for נבלה has no job of its own. So that פסוק now teaches the handle rule for נבלה, which still needed a source because of דיו. Once that is covered, the handle פסוק of נבלה is free, and it becomes the source for a rule about handles in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed (for its own subject). This is the method of moving an extra פסוק to a new job.
Apply it to another subject.
To a handle in general, meaning every case and not only נבלה.

steps.confusionAlert: This is a chain of two moves, not one. First שומר goes to the handle of נבלה. Then the handle פסוק of נבלה, which is now free, goes to handles in general.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אִם אֵין עִנְיָן לְשׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה,
phrases.english: Rather, if it is not needed for the protective covering of a carcass,
phrases.notes: This is the שומר פסוק of נבלה, which step 32 showed has no job of its own.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of the handle of a carcass,
and if it is not needed for the handle of a carcass,
phrases.notes: Now that the handle of נבלה is covered, the handle פסוק of נבלה is the one left free.

phrases.english: apply it to the matter of a handle in general.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִם אֵין עִנְיָן לְשׁוֹמֵר דִּנְבֵלָה, תְּנֵהוּ עִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer of step 32 by actually moving the extra שומר פסוק and showing where each verse ends up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moving an extra פסוק to a new subject ('אם אינו ענין') in a two-link chain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The handle פסוק of נבלה seemed to be needed for itself because of דיו, so there was no extra verse left for handles in general.
steps.terutzMaskana: The extra שומר פסוק covers the handle of נבלה, which frees the handle פסוק of נבלה to teach about handles in general.

steps.title: Summary: handle out, handle in, covering joins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sums up the final sources: a handle carries טומאה out, a handle brings טומאה in, and a שומר joins together with the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: So: a handle carries out, a handle brings in, and the protective covering joins together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a short final list of what each source teaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One handle source teaches that a handle passes טומאה out from the item to whatever touches it. Another teaches that a handle brings טומאה in to the item. The שומר source from food teaches that the covering counts together with the food to reach the needed size for טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: To carry out. Here, the handle passes טומאה from the item outward.
To bring in. Here, the handle lets טומאה come into the item.
To join together. Here, the covering counts with the food to make up the minimum size.

steps.whatToRemember: Final result: יד להוציא, יד להכניס, ושומר לצרף. Two handle sources (one for 'out', one for 'in') and one שומר source for joining. The extra verse came from the שומר of נבלה through a chain of 'אם אינו ענין'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This restores the same three-part summary as step 30, now on solid ground after the דיו objection in step 31.

phrases.english: A handle to carry out, a handle to bring in,
and the protective covering to join together.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָד לְהוֹצִיא, יָד לְהַכְנִיס, וְשׁוֹמֵר לְצָרֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the result of the chain in step 33, repeating the summary from step 30 after the objection was answered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A handle carries טומאה out, a handle brings טומאה in, and a שומר joins with the food to reach the minimum size, each with its own source.
